title: Qualitative / case study
covers: Case studies, process tracing, historical cases, interviews, focus groups, ethnography and document analysis.

adapted_from.name: Lincoln & Guba trustworthiness, as set out by Nowell et al. 2017
Gibbert, Ruigrok & Wicki 2008 (internal and construct validity)
GRADE-CERQual, adequacy of data (Lewin et al. 2018)

questions.text: Are the data sources described: who was interviewed or observed, which documents, and how many?
Is the choice of cases or participants explained, and suited to the question?
Do the conclusions stay within the cases studied, or is any wider claim argued (for example by replication across cases)?
Is the analysis described: how the data were coded, compared or traced to reach the findings?
Are the findings shown with evidence from the data: quotations, documents, events or detailed description?
Are findings checked across several sources, or are rival explanations considered?
Is there enough data for the claims made: enough cases, interviews or depth?
Do the authors state their own role or position, and the study's funding?
